title: Older scholastics vs today's schools
source_text: XXXII. Fuerunt quidem inter veteres Scholasticos qui authoritatem illam de Scriptura infallibiliter & certo determinandi ad Apostolicam Ecclesiam restrinxerunt, & docuerunt non alio sensu tribuendam esse Ecclesiae praesenti, quam quia cum Apostolica censetur unum corpus. Et senex revera fecit quae fecit quum esset puer, licet jam senex non possit amplius illa facere. Quae fuit sententia Durandi, & Thomae Waldensis, & etiam superiori saeculo Driedonis. At haec sententia hodie communiter erronea censetur. Et hodierni Scholae Pontificiae Doctores in priorem illam sententiam concedunt. Itaque videndum est, an ex usu & praxi Ecclesiae, & illis priscorum Patrum argumentationibus, quae supra adductae sunt, concludi possit Pastorum qui unoquoque saeculo Ecclesiam gubernant, authoritatem tantam esse, ut sit fidei nostrae circa Scripturam regula, Scriptura ipsa quoad nos certior & notior, & qua fides nostra de Scriptura sacra, tanquam praecipuo fundamento nitatur. Illud est quod negamus: neque quicquam ad hoc faciunt probationes illae quae supra allatae sunt.
pass_a_gloss: There were indeed among the older Scholastics those who restricted that authority of determining infallibly and certainly concerning Scripture to the Apostolic Church, and taught that it is to be attributed to the present Church in no other sense than because it is reckoned one body with the Apostolic. And an old man truly did what he did when he was a boy, although now as an old man he cannot do those things any longer. Which was the opinion of Durandus, and of Thomas of Walden, and also in the previous age of Driedo. But this opinion today is commonly judged erroneous. And the Doctors of today's Pontifician School concede to that former opinion. Therefore it must be seen whether from the use and practice of the Church, and from those argumentations of the ancient Fathers which were adduced above, it can be concluded that the authority of the Pastors who in each age govern the Church is so great that it is the rule of our faith concerning Scripture, more certain and better known to us than Scripture itself, and that on which our faith concerning sacred Scripture rests as on its chief foundation. That is what we deny: nor do those proofs which were brought above contribute anything to this.
pass_b_english: Among the older scholastics some did restrict that power of deciding Scripture infallibly and with certainty to the Apostolic Church. They taught that it belongs to the present Church only insofar as that Church is counted one body with the Apostolic — as an old man truly did what he did as a boy, though as an old man he can no longer do those same acts.

That was the view of Durandus, of Thomas Netter of Walden, and in the previous age of Driedo. Today that view is commonly judged wrong, and the doctors of the present Roman schools yield to the earlier opinion instead.

So the question is whether from the Church's practice, and from the ancient Fathers' arguments recited above, one may conclude that the pastors who govern the Church in each age have authority so great that it is our rule of faith about Scripture — more certain and better known to us than Scripture itself — and the chief foundation of our faith in sacred Scripture.
That is what we deny. The proofs already brought do nothing to establish it.
